  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35841v1</id>
    <title>Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T17:54:16Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35841v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35841v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T17:54:16Z</published>
    <arxiv:comment>10 pages</arxiv:comment>
    <arxiv:primary_category term="math.GR"/>

      <name>Jonas Pinke</name>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35674v1</id>
    <title>Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T16:16:19Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35674v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35674v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.</summary>
    <category term="math.OA" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T16:16:19Z</published>
    <arxiv:comment>57 pages. Comments welcome</arxiv:comment>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35643v1</id>
    <title>Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T15:52:18Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35643v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35643v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T15:52:18Z</published>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35623v1</id>
    <title>Generalizing Praeger--Xu graphs</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T15:38:18Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35623v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35623v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We uniformly study directed Praeger--Xu graphs and Praeger's generalized family $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$, without requiring that $s\mid r$ and $Γ$ is an undirected graph. Assuming that $Γ\times\overrightarrow{K}_2$ is connected, we determine the full automorphism group of $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ for every $r$ and $s$, prove connectivity, characterize vertex-transitivity, and give an equivalent criterion for $t$-arc-transitivity. We also study when $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ is a Cayley graph.
  We also give two applications. First, we give a new family of twin-free connected arc-transitive digraphs of valency $4$ whose vertex stabilizers have exponential growth. We also give a connected regular digraph that is not vertex-transitive but whose direct product with a directed cycle is Cayley.</summary>
    <category term="math.CO" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35603v1</id>
    <title>Modular representations of metabelian groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T15:27:08Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35603v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35603v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $φ:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+φ(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(φ)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(φ)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T15:27:08Z</published>
    <arxiv:comment>11 pages</arxiv:comment>

      <name>Lorenzo Traldi</name>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35561v1</id>
    <title>Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T15:02:07Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35561v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35561v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.</summary>
    <category term="math.PR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35537v1</id>
    <title>2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T14:50:49Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35537v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35537v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.</summary>
    <category term="math.RA" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35388v1</id>
    <title>On Cayley Graphs of Skew Braces and Their Distances</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T13:09:08Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35388v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35388v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We introduce the left and right Cayley graphs of a finite skew brace $(A,\cdot, \circ)$ with a connection set $T\subset A$, as a directed multigraph with additive and multiplicative edges, depicting the operations $\cdot$ and $\circ$ respectively. We compute the distance from $a$ to $a\circ b$ in these Cayley graphs in terms of factorization lengths over $T$. As an application, we provide a characterization of the ideals of a skew brace in terms of their corresponding Cayley graphs.</summary>
    <category term="math.CO" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35222v1</id>
    <title>The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T11:13:35Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35222v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35222v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35197v1</id>
    <title>Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T10:50:51Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35197v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35197v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.</summary>
